topIssues.title: ZKDisputeGame: a respected game can use an unrespected game as its parent
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
## Summary

A ZK game can start from its parent's claim. Its proof shows only that the transition from that claim is correct. `initialize()` checks that the parent did not lose, is not blacklisted or retired, has the same game type, and is above the anchor. It does not check the parent's `wasRespectedGameTypeWhenCreated`. `isGameClaimValid` checks only the child's flag.

So a claim that does not count, and that challengers may not watch, can become the start of a claim that counts.

## Where

- `packages/contracts-bedrock/src/dispute/zk/ZKDisputeGame.sol:346-368`: the parent checks.
- `packages/contracts-bedrock/src/dispute/AnchorStateRegistry.sol:331-353`: `isGameClaimValid`.

## Scenarios

1. **Rollout.** ZK is registered before it is respected. An attacker creates a ZK game with a forged root, and nobody challenges it. After ZK becomes respected, a respected child proves a correct transition from that forged root and becomes a valid claim.
2. **Incident.** A prestate bug forces a fallback to another game type. During the fallback, an attacker creates a ZK game that uses the bug. It is not retired, because it was created after the retirement time. After the switch back to ZK, a respected child of that game becomes a valid claim.

The FPVM games are not affected. They have no parents and always start from the anchor.

## Fix

Compute the child's respected flag first in `initialize()`. Then add:

```solidity
if (wasRespectedGameTypeWhenCreated && !parent.wasRespectedGameTypeWhenCreated()) revert InvalidParentGame();
```

Unrespected children can still use any parent, so proposal chains can continue after a switch away from ZK. Update the spec (`game-mechanics.md:124-126`) to match.

topIssues.title: kona-sp1: an omitted L2 header makes Holocene derivation skip a valid span batch
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
## Summary

When a span batch starts before the safe head, the batch stage reads the batch's parent block and the overlapped blocks through the L2 provider. If a read fails, `check_batch_prefix` or `check_batch_overlap` returns `Undecided`. Holocene's `BatchStream` has already consumed the batch, so it skips it.

In the SP1 guest, the prover controls whether a header is in the witness. The prover can omit the header of the batch's parent and make the guest skip a valid batch. No later batch covers those blocks. After the sequencing window ends, the pipeline makes empty batches, and the guest proves deposit-only blocks in place of the real ones.

## Where

- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/batch/span.rs:735-741` (prefix) and `span.rs:555-560` (overlap): a fetch error returns `Undecided`.
- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/derive/src/stages/batch/batch_stream.rs:189-193`: the span batch is skipped, not retried.
- `rust/kona/sp1/crates/client/src/witness/preimage_store.rs:80-88`: a missing key returns `Err`.

## Impact

A forged L2 history that removes all user transactions after the proof's start block. After that, a double withdrawal through an L1 deposit is possible.

- It affects every Holocene chain, with or without interop, and it does not need a malicious batcher.
- It requires a batch whose parent is older than the guest's reset walk-back. That is usual when one batch covers more than about 10 minutes of L2 blocks.
- EIP-2935 does not stop it.

The FPVM is not affected, because a Cannon preimage read cannot fail for missing data.

## Fix

Use the same guest wrapper as the ZK-01 issue: a missing preimage key panics. The retain-and-retry change in #22629 fixes op-node liveness only. It does not fix this, because a retry in the guest gets the same missing key again.

## Test

Add a regression test: a range witness without the parent header must stop the guest. Today the guest commits the output root of a deposit-only block.

topIssues.title: kona-host: add an L1 slot-duration override flag
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
kona-host learns the L1 beacon slot duration only from the beacon node's `/eth/v1/config/spec`. Both the single-chain host ([`single/cfg.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/b9ae98c8f1a6cef46576f48831a8e51c53f87023/rust/kona/bin/host/src/single/cfg.rs#L275)) and the interop host ([`interop/cfg.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/b9ae98c8f1a6cef46576f48831a8e51c53f87023/rust/kona/bin/host/src/interop/cfg.rs#L320)) call `OnlineBlobProvider::init`, which fetches it. If the beacon node serves neither `SLOT_DURATION_MS` nor `SECONDS_PER_SLOT`, or serves an unusable value, the host can't map L1 timestamps to slots and blob preimages can't be fetched.

The challenger then can't run kona-host for its games, and there is no workaround short of changing the beacon node. #23138 added the `SLOT_DURATION_MS` fallback, but a beacon node that serves neither key remains a failure mode.

Two other components already have an escape hatch:
- **op-node:** `--l1.beacon.slot-duration-override` ([`op-node/config/beacon.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/b9ae98c8f1a6cef46576f48831a8e51c53f87023/op-node/config/beacon.go#L30)).
- **kona-node:** `--l1.slot-duration-override` ([`flags/engine/providers.rs`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/b9ae98c8f1a6cef46576f48831a8e51c53f87023/rust/kona/bin/node/src/flags/engine/providers.rs#L36)).

kona-host has none.

**Scope:**
- **The flag:** add an optional slot-duration override to the kona-host CLI, for both single and interop modes. When set, it bypasses the `/eth/v1/config/spec` fetch, matching the semantics of kona-node's flag.
- **Wiring:** pass it through `OnlineBlobProvider` initialisation.
- **sp1 crates:** update `InteropHost` construction in [`rust/kona/sp1/crates/super-range-executor`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/b9ae98c8f1a6cef46576f48831a8e51c53f87023/rust/kona/sp1/crates/super-range-executor/src/lib.rs#L714), which builds the struct field by field.
- **op-zk-proposer** expose the option and forward it to `kona_host::InteropHost` during witness collection.
- **op-challenger:** expose the option and forward it to kona-host in [`kona_server_executor.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/b9ae98c8f1a6cef46576f48831a8e51c53f87023/op-challenger/game/fault/trace/vm/kona_server_executor.go#L33) and [`kona_super_server_executor.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/b9ae98c8f1a6cef46576f48831a8e51c53f87023/op-challenger/game/fault/trace/vm/kona_super_server_executor.go#L34), alongside `--l1-beacon-address`.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topIssues.title: op-node: static peer cannot be re-dialed after its peerstore address TTL expires ("no addresses")
topIssues.author: tuan-phan
topIssues.body:
**Bug Description**

`op-node` adds the addresses of each `--p2p.static` peer to the peerstore once, at startup, with a 7-day TTL (`op-node/p2p/host.go`, `initStaticPeers`). The reconnect loop (`monitorStaticPeers` -> `dialStaticPeer`) dials by peer ID only and never re-adds the configured addresses. Once the process has been up for more than 7 days, the first disconnect from a static peer is therefore permanent: every minute the node logs

```
lvl=warn msg="static peer disconnected, reconnecting" peer=<peer-id>
lvl=info msg="dialing static peer" peer=<peer-id> addrs=[/ip4/<ip>/tcp/9222]
lvl=warn msg="error reconnecting to static peer" peer=<peer-id> err="failed to dial <peer-id>: no addresses"
```

The `addrs` printed in the log come from the CLI config, but `DialPeer` only sees the peerstore, whose entry for the peer has expired, hence `no addresses`. If the static peer does not advertise a dialable address of its own through identify, nothing repopulates the peerstore. Restarting op-node makes the peer dialable again because `initStaticPeers` runs again.

On a chain whose recommended node configuration is a single `--p2p.static` sequencer peer plus `--p2p.no-discovery`, this leaves the node with zero gossip peers: it stops receiving unsafe payloads, the unsafe head falls back to what L1 derivation yields (minutes behind the sequencer tip) and `optimism_syncStatus` reports `unsafe_l2 == safe_l2`. We hit this on several nodes at once after the sequencer peer closed its connections, about a week after the nodes had started; nodes restarted the day before reconnected without any issue.

#12113 reports the same symptom (same log lines, "restarting the validator node allows it to reconnect again"); the 7-day TTL explains why it only shows up on nodes with long uptimes.

**Steps to Reproduce**

1. Start op-node with `--p2p.static=/ip4/<ip>/tcp/<port>/p2p/<peer-id>`. Adding `--p2p.no-discovery` makes the impact visible (no other peers), but is not needed for the dial failure itself.
2. Keep it running for more than 7 days, so the static peer addresses expire from the peerstore.
3. Have the static peer close the connection (restart it, or disconnect from its side).
4. Watch the op-node log: the reconnect attempt fails every minute with `failed to dial <peer-id>: no addresses`, and `opp2p_peers` reports `totalConnected: 0` when there are no other peers.

The same failure can be reproduced in a unit test without waiting 7 days, by clearing the static peer's addresses from the peerstore after a disconnect and calling `dialStaticPeer` again; on `develop` it fails with exactly `failed to dial <peer-id>: no addresses`. A PR with that test and a fix follows.

**Expected behavior**

The configured addresses of a static peer are available for every reconnect attempt, so a static peer can be re-dialed for as long as the process runs, regardless of uptime.

**Environment Information:**

- Operating System: Linux (containers on Kubernetes), amd64
- Package Version: op-node v1.19.7 and v1.19.8; the relevant code in `op-node/p2p/host.go` is unchanged on `develop` (dfe4f947)

**Configurations:**

```
--p2p.static=/ip4/<ip>/tcp/9222/p2p/<peer-id>
--p2p.no-discovery
--p2p.listen.tcp=9222
--p2p.advertise.ip=<public-ip>
--p2p.peerstore.path=/data/op-node/peer
--p2p.discovery.path=/data/op-node/discovery
```

**Logs:**

See the block above; it repeats once per minute until op-node is restarted. On the same node, `optimism_syncStatus` shows `unsafe_l2` equal to `safe_l2` and several minutes old, and `opp2p_peers` shows `totalConnected: 0`.

**Additional context**

Workaround without a restart: `opp2p_connectPeer` with the full multiaddr of the static peer, since `host.Connect` re-adds the addresses before dialing. The proper fix is to re-add the configured addresses in `dialStaticPeer` before `DialPeer`.

topPRs.title: Glamsterdam L1 Upgrade Compatibility
topPRs.author: max-sanchez
topPRs.body:
Sepolia activates Glamsterdam ("Amsterdam" on the execution layer) on
  2026-10-06 13:53:36 UTC. This PR keeps op-node, op-batcher and op-proposer
  working when the L1 under them forks. The L2 does not activate any Amsterdam
  feature.

  Depends on hemilabs/op-geth#111, pinned here at f5c491e251ce, which adds the
  two new L1 header fields with codecs identical to upstream v1.17.7.

  ## Changes

  - **Pin op-geth f5c491e251ce** and adapt to its API (gas-limit-aware
    `ValidateOptimismExtraData` at every call site, `SetCode`/`SetBalance`
    reasons, `ChainContext` stubs, `NewBlockChain` signature).
  - **`RPCHeader` carries `blockAccessListHash` and `slotNumber`**, so op-node's
    L1 block hash verification (and the head subscription) keeps working from
    the fork block on. Without this every post-fork block fails verification and
    derivation stops.
  - **Batcher calldata gas limit** is the larger of the old and the Amsterdam
    floor (15000 + 64 gas/byte), valid on both sides of the fork. Blob
    transactions are unaffected.
  - **Beacon spec**: read `SLOT_DURATION_MS` with a fallback to
    `SECONDS_PER_SLOT` (port of upstream #23138).
  - A guard in `RPCBlock.ExecutionPayloadEnvelope` against blocks with the new
    fields, tests for the gas-limit wiring, and fixed stale test call sites.

  Receipts, deposits, the L1 attributes deposit and the proposer were traced and
  tested and need no change.

  ## Verification
  
  - Unit tests with an upstream v1.17.7 header fixture; all 53,300 Amsterdam
    headers from execution-spec-tests through every L1 header path, 0 mismatches.
  - The op-node L1 client with full verification against the live Glamsterdam
    devnet: 472 blocks across its fork boundary, 26,071 receipts, tx types 0 to 4.
  - Every batcher transaction shape accepted by upstream v1.17.7 under Amsterdam
    rules and by Hemi's op-geth under Osaka rules.
  - Six review rounds (three on this branch, three cross-cutting).
  - The heminetwork localnet (branch `max/glamsterdam-l1-migration-e2e`) now
    forks the L1 while the stack runs, with hash verification on, in blob and
    calldata mode. It passes with this branch.

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock,op-core,op-supernode,kona: formal models and differential tests for interop message expiry
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Adds formal models, symbolic checks and differential tests for interop message expiry and `SuperchainETHBridge` refunds (#23259). They give reviewers machine-checked evidence that the shipped design cannot pay ETH twice: a message is never both relayed on its destination and refunded on its source. These models found the pre-staged-withdrawal double spend in the earlier design, where L1 trusted the L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger as the sender. That finding is why exports now come from the `UndeliveredMessageExporter` predeploy. They check that the landed design closes the gap. Without them, the safety argument rests on prose and unit tests.

No effect on users: everything is test or verification code. The Solidity under `test/formal/` compiles into the forge test build, and its Foundry invariant and fuzz suites run in contracts-bedrock CI with inline budgets. The Lean, Quint, Dafny, Halmos, Kontrol, hevm and EVMLean harnesses are not wired into CI; each directory's README says how to run it. The three Go/Rust tests run the real window-rule implementations against shared vectors.

The files live in a new `test/formal/expiry/` tree rather than `test/invariants/` and `test/kontrol/` because one argument spans several tools. `test/formal/expiry/README.md` maps each property to the tools that check it, and lists what is proved and what is assumed. The one-line `test-validation` exclusion is needed because these files have no matching `src/` path, as for `test/invariants/`.

Related: #23259.

Reviews: each layer was audited by a fresh-context reviewer and by two independent model reviewers; the outcomes are in each README's review log. `go-code-reviewer` and `rust-code-reviewer` are pending for the differential tests. `interop-reviewer` and `/security-review` are not run because this diff changes no production code; they apply to #23259.

topPRs.title: op-deployer: share one bootstrapped L1 across PCD test cases
topPRs.author: maurelian
topPRs.body:
`TestCLIPCDResume` ran a full Anvil + `bootstrap superchain` + `bootstrap implementations` for each of its nine cases, and `TestCLIPCDJourney` for each of its two. The bootstrap pair is the slowest op-deployer operation and nothing under test mutates it, so it now runs once per test function.

`pcdBootstrappedL1` holds the bootstrapped L1 and hands each case a fresh CLI runner and workdir on it. `newJourney` first reverts the L1 to a post-bootstrap snapshot, restoring the deployer nonce, block height, and any injected code — so the existing absolute-nonce assertions and `postBootstrapL1State` baseline hold unchanged, and rerunning a failed case is now idempotent.

`TestCLIPCDBoot` keeps its own L1; it needs a Prague-specific Anvil.

Measured locally, same synthetic prestate for both runs:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `TestCLIPCDResume` | 398.9s | 95.6s |
| `TestCLIPCDJourney` | 89.7s | 51.1s |

That is ~5.7 min off the `go-tests` shard, which runs this package under a 40m budget.

Targets `test/pcd-e2e-integration` (#22356).

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock,op-core,op-interop-filter,kona!: per-message interop expiry and SuperchainETHBridge refunds
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Interop executing messages can't be forced in through deposits, so a destination sequencer that refuses to relay a message can keep it from ever being delivered. For `SuperchainETHBridge.sendETH`, that strands the ETH: it is burned on the source chain and never minted on the destination.

This PR lets the source chain learn, through censorship-resistant paths only, that a message can never be delivered. It exposes that per message as `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger.expiredMessages(messageHash)`. `SuperchainETHBridge.refundETH` uses it to give the ETH back.

It replaces #22601, rebuilt on current `develop`. There is no registry, no admin setter, no app callback and no configurable window.

BREAKING CHANGE: `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger.resendMessage` is removed, and the messenger now rejects messages whose target is the `L2CrossDomainMessenger` or the `L2ToL1MessagePasser` (`MessageTargetUnsafe`).
- **Who is affected:** applications and relayers that resend unrelayed interop messages, and anyone sending cross-chain messages to those two targets.
- **What breaks:** a message that isn't relayed within the expiry window can no longer be revived.
- **Configuration:** op-core and kona now refuse to load a dependency set whose `overrideMessageExpiryWindow` exceeds 604800 seconds (7 days), and `op-interop-filter` refuses `--message-expiry-window` above 168h. Operators with a longer override must lower it.
- **Migration:** treat an unrelayed message as expired, and undo the send on the source chain after `expiredMessages(messageHash)` is set, as `SuperchainETHBridge.refundETH` does. To reach L1 or the L2 messenger from a relayed message, go through your own contract.

## The protocol fact it builds on

An executing message is invalid when its block is more than the message expiry window (7 days) after its initiating message's block. Both cross-safety (op-supernode) and the fault proof (kona) enforce this, comparing the same two timestamps.

So once a destination's clock passes `sendTime + window` and the message is still unrelayed, no valid block can relay it. This PR carries that fact back to the source chain over a withdrawal followed by a deposit.

## How it works

For a message `H` sent from A to B and never relayed on B:

1. **On A, at send time:** `sendMessage` stores `sentMessageTimestamps[H] = block.timestamp`.
2. **On B, export:** anyone calls `UndeliveredMessageExporter.exportUndeliveredMessage(sourceMessenger, source, nonce, sender, target, message, minGasLimit)`. This is a new predeploy at `0x…0030`.
   - It hashes the message with **B's own chain ID as the destination**, so a chain can only speak for messages addressed to it.
   - It requires `!L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger.successfulMessages(H)`.
   - It sends `relayUndeliveredMessage(H, block.timestamp)` to `sourceMessenger`, which is A's `L1CrossDomainMessenger`, through the `L2CrossDomainMessenger`.
   - This is not an executing message, so if B censors it, it can be forced in as a deposit. The acceptance test does exactly that.
3. **On L1:** B's `L1CrossDomainMessenger` relays the withdrawal into A's `L1CrossDomainMessenger.relayUndeliveredMessage`. The function first requires that A has the `INTEROP` feature enabled. It then accepts the call only if:
   - the caller is a real `L1CrossDomainMessenger`: its portal's `SystemConfig` names it as that chain's messenger;
   - the caller's portal is authorized by **A's `ETHLockbox`**, meaning it is in A's cluster;
   - the L2 sender of the withdrawal is the **`UndeliveredMessageExporter`**.

   It then sends `expireMessage(H, undeliveredAt)` to A's `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger` as a deposit.
4. **On A, expire:** `expireMessage` accepts only the `L2CrossDomainMessenger` relaying from A's own `L1CrossDomainMessenger`, which is `otherMessenger()`, so L2 needs no new address. If `undeliveredAt > sentMessageTimestamps[H] + EXPIRY_PERIOD`, it sets `expiredMessages[H] = true`.
5. **On A, refund:** anyone calls `SuperchainETHBridge.refundETH(destination, nonce, from, to, amount)`. It rebuilds `H` from those arguments, requires `expiredMessages[H]`, and refunds `from` exactly once with a forced send.

**Why a refund can't double-spend:** B attests that H was unrelayed at a time past the window, and from then on the protocol rejects any relay of H. A acts only on a fact dated past `EXPIRY_PERIOD`, measured from a send time that is written once and never changes.

### Why the trusted sender is a new predeploy

The L1 side trusts withdrawals from the `UndeliveredMessageExporter` at `0x…0030`. It does not trust the `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger`.
- **No forged withdrawal can predate the upgrade.** The proxy at `0x…0030` had no implementation until this upgrade, so no withdrawal from it exists from before.
- **It can't be impersonated.** The exporter makes exactly one kind of call, so nothing can make it say something it didn't check.

The messenger, by contrast, has a history of relaying messages to arbitrary targets. Trusting it would let forged withdrawals created before the upgrade wait in unfinalized withdrawals or failed messages and be replayed afterwards. It would also open a window during any L1-before-L2 rollout.

### What prevents each attack
- **Forged facts from other chains:** every chain whose portal A's lockbox authorizes can already withdraw A's ETH, so trusting its facts adds no trust.
- **A forged messenger borrowing a real portal:** it fails the reverse binding.
- **Governance of another cluster chain:** that chain's governance could upgrade its own exporter and forge facts about any destination. That is the same trust as the shared `ETHLockbox` already places in it, since lockbox portals must share one proxy admin owner.
- **Something else sending the deposit as A's L1 messenger:** `L1CrossDomainMessenger` already refuses to relay messages that target itself, so only `relayUndeliveredMessage` can make it the sender.
- **The L1 call runs out of gas:** it lands in the calling messenger's failed messages, and anyone can replay it.
- **The wrong source messenger is named:** the deposit reverts on a chain that never sent `H`, and anyone can export again.
- **A fact that arrives too early:** it fails on A with `MessageNotExpired`. It can never succeed later, because its timestamp is fixed.

## Behavior changes (please review these closely)

- **`resendMessage` is removed** (`L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger` 2.0.0).
  - **Why:** resending lets a message be relayed for another window, which conflicts with expiry: a sender could resend, take a refund, and then have the resent event relayed. And letting anyone resend would let anyone stop a message from ever expiring.
  - **What happens instead:** an unrelayed message expires, and the app undoes the send.
  - **Who loses out:** apps without a refund, such as `SuperchainTokenBridge` today, lose the ability to revive an unrelayed message until they add one. See follow-ups.
- **The messenger refuses unsafe targets.** It won't send or relay messages whose target is the `L2CrossDomainMessenger` or the `L2ToL1MessagePasser` (`MessageTargetUnsafe`).
  - **This is defense in depth:** expiry's safety doesn't depend on it.
  - **What it guarantees:** the messenger never starts a withdrawal. Nothing that trusts it as a withdrawal sender, today or in future L1 contracts, can be fooled by a relayed message.
- **The expiry window can't exceed 7 days.** op-core and kona both reject a dependency-set message expiry window override above 7 days, and `op-interop-filter` caps its `--message-expiry-window` flag the same way. A window longer than the contract's period would allow a refund followed by a valid relay.
- **`EXPIRY_PERIOD = 8 days`:** the protocol's 7-day window plus a 1-day safety margin.
- **Every message costs more gas:** `sendMessage` stores a timestamp, about 22k more gas per message.
- **Old messages can't expire:** messages sent before this upgrade have no timestamp.

## Contract changes

- **`L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger` 1.3.2 → 2.0.0:**
  - new constant `EXPIRY_PERIOD`;
  - new storage at slots 3–4: `sentMessageTimestamps` and `expiredMessages`;
  - new function `expireMessage`, the unsafe-target helper, and `resendMessage` removed;
  - no initializer, so it is still upgraded with plain `upgradeTo`.
- **New `UndeliveredMessageExporter` 1.0.0 at `0x…0030`:** gated on interop like the other interop predeploys, and wired through `Predeploys`, `L2Genesis`, `L2ContractsManager` (now 1.15.0), the Go predeploy registry and the NUT bundle.
- **`L1CrossDomainMessenger` 2.11.1 → 2.12.0:** adds `relayUndeliveredMessage`, with no new storage and an `INTEROP` gate. `EXPIRE_MESSAGE_GAS_LIMIT = 100_000`, which a cold-storage relay test exercises.
- **`SuperchainETHBridge` 1.0.1 → 1.1.0:** `sendETH` is unchanged. Adds `refundETH` and a `refunded` mapping.
- **Off-chain:** the window cap in op-core (Go), kona (Rust) and `op-interop-filter`.
- **Docs:** `message-expiration.mdx` and the interop overview now describe expiry instead of resend.

## Launch checklist

- **The window cap is live before expiry is relied on.** Every node and the accepted proof program must enforce the dependency-set window cap of 7 days or less. With an older prestate that accepts a longer override, a refund could be followed by a valid relay.
- **The dependency set and the lockbox agree.** Every chain in a cluster's dependency set must also be authorized in the cluster's `ETHLockbox` and run the exporter, in the same fork. Otherwise sends to it can't be refunded.
- **Embed each cluster's dependency set in the prestate.** It must be in the registry and the absolute prestate: kona falls back to a host-supplied dependency set for clusters that aren't in the registry.
- **Re-snapshot Lagoon after merge.** Lagoon's NUT bundle (`op-core/nuts/fork_lock.toml`) still locks the old messenger. It must be re-snapshotted once this merges, together with kona's bundle counts, and the exporter added back to op-core's `Predeploys` map at that snapshot. It is deliberately left out until then, so the frozen fork state stays unchanged.
- **Rules every future upgrade must keep:**
  - nothing may re-emit `SentMessage` for a message that already has a timestamp: no resend, and no rollback to an implementation that has `resendMessage`;
  - every way of relaying on the destination must set `successfulMessages`;
  - any change to message hashing or nonce versioning must be mirrored in the exporter.

  Breaking any of these allows a refund followed by a relay.
- **Use enough L1 gas when finalizing an export,** at least 1M. Because a failed relay is stored rather than reverted, `eth_estimateGas` under-estimates.

## Limitations

- **Messages sent before the upgrade can't be recovered.** They have no send timestamp, so they can never expire, and with `resendMessage` gone they can't be resent either. In production this ships with interop's launch, so no messages predate it.
- **`refundETH` always pays `from`,** which is `sendETH`'s `msg.sender`. A router that sent ETH on someone's behalf needs its own way to pass a refund on. If `sendETH` was itself called from a relayed interop message, `from` is the `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger`, and a refund would be stuck there.
- **An early export is harmless.** It fails on the source with `MessageNotExpired`. Export again after `EXPIRY_PERIOD`.

## Testing

- **Forge:**
  - messenger: send timestamps, the unsafe-target rule on send and on relay, `expireMessage` auth and the exact boundary, and `expireMessage` through a real `L2CrossDomainMessenger` relay with cold storage, including an out-of-gas run then a replay;
  - exporter: hashing, the delivered check, and an export forced in from a deposit;
  - `L1CrossDomainMessenger`: an integration test with real contracts; rejection of a forged messenger, another lockbox, the wrong L2 sender (including `0x…23`), interop disabled, and the chain's own messenger;
  - bridge: refund after expiry pays exactly once; a forged refund through a direct `sendMessage` reverts; wrong-preimage fuzzing;
  - one end-to-end test of send → export → L1 → expire → refund, using `vm.warp`.
- **Acceptance (`op-acceptance-tests/tests/interop/expiry`, two-chain interop devnet):** every leg runs for real:
  - `sendETH` from A, never relayed on B;
  - an export **forced in as an L1 deposit** on B;
  - prove and finalize, then A's L1 messenger relays and the deposit lands on A.

  The devnet can't advance L2 time 8 days, so the test then asserts the exact `MessageNotExpired` rejection, the carried hash and the timestamp. Forge covers the expired path. The acceptance test also checks ordinary relays and that exporting a delivered message is refused.
- **Go and Rust:** tests for the window cap, and tests pinning the constants.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- A spec section.
- Refunds in `SuperchainTokenBridge`, using the same `expiredMessages` check.
- Formal models and proofs, in a stacked draft PR: Lean, Quint, Kontrol, Halmos and invariant fuzzing.

topPRs.title: contracts-bedrock: Per-chain Review Period
topPRs.author: 0xarktos
topPRs.body:
Closes [#686](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism-private/issues/686)

## Description

Makes the withdrawal review period configurable per chain. `PROOF_MATURITY_DELAY_SECONDS` (OptimismPortal2) and `DISPUTE_GAME_FINALITY_DELAY_SECONDS` (AnchorStateRegistry) move from constructor immutables on the shared implementations to per-chain proxy storage, set at `initialize()` and changeable through an L1PAO-only setter. The implementations keep a min/max pair of constructor immutables that bound every write.

OPCM carries each chain's live value forward on upgrade. The Migrator preserves each portal's and legacy registry's value and gives the shared AnchorStateRegistry the value the legacy registries agree on. op-deployer takes the delays as per-chain inputs and the bounds as implementation inputs.

Of the ~2,000 lines added, 786 are Solidity tests, 183 are regenerated snapshots, and most of the 576 Go lines are gofmt realignment of struct literals that gained the longer bound field names. The reviewable contract change is ~460 lines.

## Design decisions

- Storage, not immutables: `proofMaturityDelaySeconds` lands in portal slot 64 and `disputeGameFinalityDelaySeconds` in registry slot 7, both tagged `@custom:network-specific`. The existing getters keep their selectors, so every reader of the delays is unaffected.

- `initialize()` and the setter share one internal `_set…` that bounds-checks, stores and emits the `…Set` event, following `SystemConfig._setGasLimit`.

- Bounds are constructor immutables with getters, standard `[1 d, 7 d]` for proof maturity and `[12 h, 3.5 d]` for the finality delay. The constructor and `DeployImplementations` reject `min == 0` and `min > max`; there is no chain-id floor in the deploy script, since VerifyOPCM checks the bound immutables at release and the StandardValidator pins the implementation.

- No `upgrade` override for the delays due to the contract size limit on the OPCM. `_loadFullConfig` reads the live getters and passes them back to `initialize()`; `overrides.cfg.proofMaturityDelaySeconds` / `…disputeGameFinalityDelaySeconds` are not allow-listed and are rejected as unknown instructions. The setters are the only write path after deployment; For atomic upgrade and delay setting batch the calls in the same superchain-ops batch.

- Due to the contract size limit, OPCM does not validate the delays and the values are checked directly on the implementation.

- It is assumed that on the time of interop migration, chains will share the same delays. The shared ASR is initialized with the finality delay every chain's registry reports, or `migrate()` reverts with `OPContractsManagerMigrator_DisputeGameFinalityDelayMismatch` before any portal is touched. The shared-registry `initialize` moved into `_initializeSharedAnchorStateRegistry` because evaluating the agreement check inline in `migrate()` hits stack-too-deep.

- `StandardValidator` gains range checks (`PORTAL-100`, `…-ANCHORP-80`): "standard" now means within the sanctioned range. `VerifyOPCM` verifies the bound immutables on the implementations (`EXPECTED_MIN_/MAX_…` env vars with standard defaults) instead of a delay value the implementation no longer holds.

- op-deployer: the delays move from `SuperchainProofParams` to `ChainProofParams` under the same JSON keys, so existing `globalDeployOverrides` keep working and per-chain `deployOverrides` can differ; the bounds take their place as implementation inputs. `op-devstack` and `op-e2e` widen the bounds for their short devnet delays.

- Versions: OptimismPortal2 6.0.0, AnchorStateRegistry 5.0.0 (constructor and `initialize` ABI change, reinit versions bumped), OPContractsManagerStandardValidator 4.1.0, OPCM V2 9.0.3 (lands in the in-development 9.x release).

## Tests

Contracts, from `packages/contracts-bedrock`:

- `just pr` — build, lint, snapshots, semver-lock, interfaces, spacers, semgrep, size check.
- `just test-dev --match-contract 'OptimismPortal2_|AnchorStateRegistry_|OPContractsManagerV2_Deploy_Test|OPContractsManagerStandardValidator_|DeployImplementations_|DeployOPChain_|VerifyOPCM_|Initializable_|SetDisputeGameImpl'` — setter and `initialize` matrix (access control, bounds, events), delay changes applied to already-proven withdrawals and already-resolved games, deploy stores the delays in proxy storage, bounds errors on deploy, rejected override keys, StandardValidator range codes, VerifyOPCM bound checks.
- `DEV_FEATURE__OPTIMISM_PORTAL_INTEROP=true just test-dev --match-contract OPContractsManagerV2_Migrate_Test` — portal and legacy-registry delays preserved, shared registry inherits the agreed value, mismatch reverts.
- `just test-dev --match-path test/invariants/OptimismPortal2.t.sol` — the ProxyAdmin owner is excluded as a sender so the fuzzer cannot move the window under the invariants.
- `just test-upgrade` (needs `ETH_RPC_URL`) — `test_upgrade_withdrawalDelaysUnchangedWithoutOverride_succeeds` proves the 7 d / 3.5 d carry-forward through the real upgrade path.

Go, from the repo root:

- `just lint-go` passes.
- `go test ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/opcm/... ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/pipeline/... ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/state/... ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/bootstrap/ ./op-chain-ops/interopgen/...` — struct mirrors load against the current script ABIs on both the script-host and forge paths, `ResolveChainProofParams` defaults and per-chain overrides, bootstrap `Check()` bound cases.
- `go test ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/integration_test/ -run TestProofParamOverrides` — bounds verified as implementation immutables, delays verified in portal slot 64 and registry slot 7 of the deployed proxies.

## Additional context

`op-deployer bootstrap implementations` replaces `--proof-maturity-delay-seconds` and `--dispute-game-finality-delay-seconds` with `--min-/--max-proof-maturity-delay-seconds` and `--min-/--max-dispute-game-finality-delay-seconds` (env `…_MIN_/MAX_…`). Operators who set the delays through `globalDeployOverrides` are unaffected; the keys now configure the chain rather than the implementation. Chains whose live delay is outside the bounds cannot upgrade until they redeploy; every production chain is at 7 d / 3.5 d.

- [Design doc](https://app.notion.com/p/oplabs/Per-chain-airgap-and-DelayedWETH-delay-proposed-changes-and-design-3e5f153ee162809ca7ebc1cf92d1e2ab)
